subject.title: fix(config): restore redacted array values by item identity

question: When an edited redacted array contains an existing visible ID, should that always mean the original row was retained, or must the Control UI provide separate row-continuity data so reusing an ID cannot adopt the removed row’s secret?
rationale: The submitted payload contains only the configured ID and redacted placeholder, so the server cannot infer whether an ID denotes retention or a different row renamed to a removed ID. Choosing either behavior establishes a durable config and credential-restoration contract.

options.title: Add row-continuity data
options.body: Extend the Control UI save contract so restore can reject reused IDs while continuing to preserve secrets for truly retained rows.

options.title: Define ID reuse as adoption
options.body: Treat an existing ID as the same logical row and document/test that reusing it intentionally retains the original row’s redacted values.

options.title: Defer identity restoration
options.body: Pause this branch until the product contract is chosen, keeping the linked bug open rather than merging a partial fix with an undocumented credential-binding edge case.

recommendation.title: Add row-continuity data
recommendation.body: Extend the Control UI save contract so restore can reject reused IDs while continuing to preserve secrets for truly retained rows.
